# Baruch Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_004_page_001.jpg

---

**1** She is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures forever; all who hold her fast will live, and those who forsake her will die.

**2** Turn, O Jacob, and take hold of her; walk toward her light, toward the brightness of her fires.

**3** Do not give your glory to another or your advantages to a foreign people.

**4** Blessed are we, O Israel, for we know what is pleasing to God.

**5** Take courage, my people, O memorial of Israel!

**6** You were sold to the nations, not for destruction, but because you provoked God to anger; and you were delivered up to your adversaries.

**7** For you provoked the one who made you by sacrificing to demons and not to God.

**8** You forgot the eternal God who nourished you, and you grieved Jerusalem who nursed you.

**9** For she saw the wrath that came upon you from God, and she said: Listen, you neighbors of Zion! God has brought great mourning upon me,

**10** for I have seen the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal brought upon them.

**11** For I nourished them with joy; but I sent them away with weeping and mourning.

**12** Let no one rejoice over me, a widow and forsaken by many; I have been left desolate because of the sins of my children, because they turned away from the law of God,

**13** and did not know his statutes and did not walk in the ways of God's commandments, and did not tread the paths of discipline in his righteousness.

**14** Let the neighbors of Zion come; remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal brought upon them.

**15** For he brought upon them a nation from far away, a shameless nation of strange language, which had no respect for an old man and took no pity on a child.

**16** They took away the widow's beloved sons, and left her who was alone bereft of her daughters.

**17** But I, how can I help you?

**18** For the one who brought these calamities upon you will deliver you from the hand of your enemies.

**19** Go your way, my children, go your way; for I am left desolate.

**20** I have put off the robe of peace and put on the sackcloth of petition; I will cry to the Eternal all my days.

**21** Take courage, my children; cry to God, and he will deliver you from the power and the hand of the enemies.

**22** For I have put my hope in the Eternal for your salvation, and joy has come to me from the Holy One, because of the mercy that will speedily come to you from your eternal savior.

**23** For I sent you out with mourning and weeping, but God will give you back to me with joy and gladness forever.

**24** For as the neighbors of Zion have now seen your captivity, so they will speedily see your salvation by God, which will come upon you with great glory and splendor of the Eternal.

**25** My children, endure with patience the wrath that has come upon you from God; your enemy has overtaken you, but you will soon see his destruction and will tread upon their necks.

**26** My tender children walked on rough paths; they were taken away like a flock carried off by enemies.

**27** Take courage, my children, and cry to God, for you will be remembered by the one who brought this upon you.

**28** For just as it was your will to go astray from God, return with tenfold zeal to seek him.

**29** For the one who brought these calamities upon you will bring you everlasting joy with your salvation.

**30** Take courage, O Jerusalem; the one who gave you that name will comfort you.

**31** Wretched are those who afflicted you and rejoiced at your fall.

**32** Wretched are the cities that your children served; wretched is the one that received your sons.

**33** For as she rejoiced at your fall and was glad for your ruin, so she will be grieved at her own desolation.

**34** And I will take away her pride in her great population, and her boastfulness will be turned to mourning.

**35** For fire will come upon her from the Eternal for many days, and for a long time she will be inhabited by demons.

**36** Look toward the east, O Jerusalem, and see the joy that is coming to you from God!

**37** See, your sons are coming, whom you sent away; they are coming, gathered from east to west, at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.

---
*EMET notes: v.1 is a continuation from ch.3:38 in the Greek — the chapter break is editorial. v.7 "demons" for daimoniois — a clear LXX echo of Deut 32:17 (they sacrificed to demons). v.8 "the eternal God" — ho aiōnios — this divine epithet is characteristic of Baruch and may reflect the Hebrew le-'olam. v.20 "robe of peace" — the peaceful garment theme will be reversed in ch.5:1-2. v.25 "tread upon their necks" — aggressive military imagery preserved.*
